newsitem.title: USA: Four Corners 750 MW coal-fired unit restarted.
newsitem.headline: Four Corners 750 MW coal-fired unit restarted.

text.p: As expected, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was restarted around 1600 MST Monday, sources familiar with the plant's operations said.
The unit, which was shut over the weekend for mechanical repairs, was expected to take several hours to ramp up to full power.
Meanwhile, Four Corners 750 MW unit 5 remained out of service for unplanned repair work which began last Tuesday.
The plant's operator said last week unit 5 would be down for at least one week and possibly three weeks, but an update on the unit's status was not available as of late Monday.
Four Corner's units 1, 2 and 3 were said to be operating near normal rates of 167 MW, 170 MW and 220 MW, respectively.
Arizona Public Service Co operates Four Corners and owns units 1, 2 and 3 along with 15 percent of units 4 and 5.
Southern California Edison Co holds a 48 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
